flags: minor: overlaps with R022-08 (both turn on the author rejecting both camps in favor of reading the whole poem); R022-08's choice B helps confirm C here
R022-01.notes: Para 4 thesis: the choice 'depends on a reading of the whole.' A and B are one-sided or too broad (no history traced); D overstates.

R022-02.notes: Para 1 says it directly. B is the first camp; C is the opposite of what the second camp wants; D twists 'cribs'.

flags: minor: overlaps with R022-04 (both rely on the wet-match example and para 3's analysis of what each version loses)
R022-03.notes: The example sets up para 3's 'Both choices lose something.' A, C (always) and D (the case is hypothetical: 'Suppose') are unsupported.

R022-04.notes: 'Vivid and strange... adds a freshness the original did not have.' A and B describe the original readers. C overstates.

R022-05.notes: A 'dead' image is one native speakers no longer notice, and it can be 'brought back to life.' C, the literal sense, is the trap.

flags: minor: choice C closely echoes the passage ('a stove that will not catch' becomes 'a stove that will not light'), which makes the application easier
minor: overlaps with R022-07, since both test para 4
R022-06.notes: Para 4: if the poem returns to fire, keep the match. B is the case for 'I feel low'; D is the opposite; A is not the author's criterion.

R022-07.notes: Para 3 shows that both choices lose something; para 4 offers 'the way out', a criterion for choosing. A: para 4 gives no contradicting example. B and C are unsupported.

flags: minor: choice B nearly repeats para 5 ('mistaken a method for a principle')
R022-08.notes: The author criticizes both camps; A and C each take one side; D contradicts the author's view that choices can be made well or badly.

R022-09.notes: A translation embodies an interpretation that can be 'judged only by returning to the evidence' (the poem). D is a tempting trap from 'the old argument never ends', but the author says translations can be judged, so the matter can be settled. B and C are unsupported.
